fomc-2026-12.standing: The Federal Reserve's rate-setting committee, which meets eight times a year to set the overnight rate US banks lend at. Its decisions price dollar borrowing worldwide, from American mortgages to emerging-market debt.
fomc-2026-12.recent: US inflation hit 3.8% in October, and the minutes showed almost all officials expect more rate hikes. The open question is size: Goolsbee left a larger-than-usual rise on the table, while CME FedWatch shows zero chance of a half-point move. The committee also meets under a probe into Bowman addressing bankers the day after a rate vote.

g20-2026-miami.standing: The annual meeting of leaders of the world's largest economies, hosted by the member holding the rotating presidency. Its members produce about 85% of global output, and its communiqué sets shared lines on trade and debt.
g20-2026-miami.recent: The US presidency convenes it after Trump's Shenzhen summit with Xi and Putin, billed as a nuclear summit, brought three of its leaders to one table, and after COP31 deadlocked over a fossil-fuel transition and finance for developing economies. What this summit settles is whether either thread reaches the wider group.

ecb-2026-12.standing: The European Central Bank's Governing Council, which meets eight times a year to set interest rates for the countries sharing the euro. Its deposit rate drives borrowing costs for some 350 million people, and the euro moves with it.
ecb-2026-12.recent: The council meets with its leadership settled by a deal Paris and Berlin sealed: Spain takes the presidency, and Germany the chief economist seat for Markus Brunnermeier. France's borrowing premium over Germany has hit 1.75 points, and the ECB has so far left France to markets, while Italy wants €5.9 billion from its banks next year.

boe-2026-12.standing: The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee, nine members who vote eight times a year on Bank Rate. Their decision sets the price of UK mortgages and business loans, and sterling and gilt yields move with it.
boe-2026-12.recent: UK inflation accelerated again in October and has now run above target for more than two years. That makes this the last decision of the year a test of how much longer the committee will tolerate a miss that keeps lengthening. Its vote split will show whether patience on the committee is wearing thin.

boj-2026-12.standing: The Bank of Japan's policy board, which meets eight times a year to set the country's short-term interest rate. Its decisions move the yen and the yield on Japanese government debt, and reach borrowers far beyond Japan.
boj-2026-12.recent: The yen breached 160 per dollar, and Washington confirmed it sold $500 million of euros to buy yen. The weak yen is already raising the cost of Japan's defence plan and its flagship AI project, while core inflation came in at 2.2%, below the 2.3% forecast. The board weighs a currency under strain against softer prices.

fred-us-gdp-2026-12-02.standing: The Bureau of Economic Analysis's measure of US output, published each quarter as an advance estimate and then revised twice. It sets the growth figure the Federal Reserve, Treasury yields and the dollar trade on.
fred-us-gdp-2026-12-02.recent: An upgrade to the last GDP figures has kept a December rate rise in play for the Fed, so this release lands on an open question: whether growth is strong enough to justify tightening again. With US consumers holding up against inflation into the holiday season, it tests how much of that strength holds.

fred-us-jobs-report-2026-12-04.standing: The Bureau of Labor Statistics' monthly Employment Situation report, usually out on the first Friday, counts nonfarm payrolls and sets the unemployment rate. Treasury yields, the dollar and Fed rate bets move on it within seconds.
fred-us-jobs-report-2026-12-04.recent: The Bureau of Labor Statistics publishes the month's payroll count and unemployment rate. The release settles whether hiring kept its pace or slowed, and it is the last full read on the labour market before the year closes.
